Title: How Much Land Does a Man Need
Author: Leo Tolstoy
Summary: This parable tells the story of Pahom, a peasant who believes that if he had enough land, he would be happy. He is given the opportunity to acquire as much land as he can walk around in one day, but his greed leads to tragic consequences.

Title: Daisy Miller
Author: Henry James
Summary: This novella explores the life of Daisy Miller, a young American woman traveling in Europe. Her flirtatious behavior and disregard for social conventions lead to her ostracism by the expatriate community, highlighting themes of innocence and societal expectations.

Title: The Yellow Wallpaper
Author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
Summary: This short story follows a woman undergoing a rest cure for her mental health. Confined to a room with yellow wallpaper, she descends into madness as she becomes obsessed with the wallpaper's patterns, symbolizing the oppression of women.

Title: The lifted veil
Author: George Eliot
Summary: This novella features a man named Latimer who possesses the ability to see into the future and read minds. His insights lead to despair as he grapples with the implications of his gift, particularly regarding love and fate

Title: The awakening
Author: Kate Chopin
Summary: The novel follows Edna Pontellier, a woman who struggles against the constraints of her marriage and societal expectations. Her journey of self-discovery leads her to seek independence and ultimately confronts the limitations placed on women in the 19th century.

Title: Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde
Author: Robert Louis Stevenson
Summary: This novella explores the duality of human nature through the character of Dr. Jekyll, who creates a potion that transforms him into the evil Mr. Hyde. The story examines themes of identity, morality, and the struggle between good and evil.

Title: The Anatomy of Violence
Author: Adrian Raine
Summary: This book investigates the biological and environmental factors that contribute to violent behavior. Raine combines neuroscience and psychology to explore the roots of violence and the implications for prevention and treatment.

Title: Play It as It Lays
Author: Joan Didion
Summary: This novel follows Maria Wyeth, a Hollywood actress grappling with personal and societal disillusionment. The narrative reflects on themes of identity, mental health, and the emptiness of modern life.

Title: Autumn
Author: Ali Smith
Summary: This novel reflects on the changing seasons and the passage of time through the relationship between a young woman and an elderly man. It explores themes of memory, art, and the impact of history on personal lives.

Title: Panenka
Author: A. J. Finn
Summary: This novel revolves around a former soccer player who becomes embroiled in a web of deceit and danger. The story explores themes of obsession, identity, and the consequences of past actions.

Title: Stoner
Author: John Williams
Summary: This novel tells the life story of William Stoner, a university professor whose quiet life is marked by personal and professional struggles. It explores themes of passion, failure, and the search for meaning.

Title: Beasts
Author: Joyce Carol Oates
Summary: Student becomes obsessed with her professor and his wife and delves into their society of degenerates.This collection of stories delves into the darker aspects of human nature, exploring themes of violence, identity, and the complexities of relationships.

Title: A Man Called Ove
Author: Fredrik Backman
Summary: This heartwarming story follows Ove, a curmudgeonly old man whose life changes when new neighbors move in. Through their interactions, Ove discovers the importance of community and connection, leading to moments of both humor and sadness.

Title: The True Deceiver
Author: Tove Jansson
Summary: This novel follows a young woman who becomes involved with an elderly artist. It explores themes of deception, art, and the nature of relationships.

Title: Gilead
Author: Marilynne Robinson
Summary: This novel is a letter from a dying preacher to his young son, reflecting on his life, faith, and the complexities of human existence. It explores themes of grace, redemption, and the passage of time.

Title: Flowers for Algernon
Author: Daniel Keyes
Summary: This novel follows Charlie Gordon, a man with an intellectual disability who undergoes an experimental surgery to increase his intelligence. The story explores the ethical implications of intelligence and the nature of human relationships.

Title: The bullet that missed
Author: Richard Osman
Summary: In this third installment of the Thursday Murder Club series, the elderly sleuths tackle a cold case involving a missing bullet and a decades-old murder. Their investigation leads to unexpected revelations about friendship and loyalty.

Title: There are 3 women and 4 men
Author: Jaden Payne
Summary: When Laurent’s wife, Marie, is found dead during an exhibition opening at the museum in 1967, the police are quick to determine suicide. Laurent is quick to determine otherwise. He promptly closes his historic building and halts his highly coveted life in the arts to dedicate the next ten years to one thing: finding the person who killed Marie.

Title: Game over girl
Author: Naomi Gibson
Summary: follows the story of Lola, a teenager who is selected to test a virtual reality (VR) game called Better Than Life at her new boarding school. The premise of the game is simple: players can create their ideal lives, but there is one crucial rule—do not recreate real people, places, or memories. However, Lola breaks this rule by constructing a version of her childhood home, which she left under mysterious circumstances.

Title: Lights all night long
Author: Lydia Fitzpatrick
Summary: tells the story of a Russian exchange student who comes to America to find his brother, who has been implicated in a crime. The narrative explores themes of family, identity, and the immigrant experience.

Title: The only one left
Author: Riley Sager
Summary: a caregiver is assigned to a woman who was once accused of a notorious murder. As she uncovers the truth, she must confront her own demons and the dark history of the family.

Title: The night shift
Author: Alex finlay
Summary: revolves around a series of murders that occur during the night shift at a local ice cream shop. The story intertwines the lives of the victims and the detectives trying to solve the case.

Title: Devil house
Author: John Darnielle
Summary: explores the haunting legacy of a murder that took place in a house that has become a tourist attraction. The narrative blends horror with psychological insights into the nature of evil.

Title: Someone knows
Author: Lisa Scottsline
Summary: Revolves around a group of friends who are haunted by a tragic event from their past. As secrets unravel, they must confront the consequences of their actions.

Title: Go ask alice
Author: Anonymous
Summary: This controversial novel presents the diary of a teenage girl who becomes addicted to drugs. It serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of substance abuse and the struggles of adolescence.

Title: Confessions
Author: Kanae Minato
Summary: This novel tells the story of a teacher seeking revenge on the students she believes are responsible for her daughter's death. The narrative is a complex exploration of guilt, morality, and the consequences of revenge.

Title: Romanovs
Author: Simon Sebag
Summary: This detailed account of the Romanov dynasty explores the lives of the last imperial family of Russia. It delves into their tragic fate and the historical context of their reign.

Title: People like her
Author: Ellery Lloyd
Summary: This novel examines the life of a social media influencer and the dark side of fame. It explores themes of identity, obsession, and the impact of online personas on real life.

Title: The secret history
Author: Donna Tartt
Summary: This novel follows a group of elite college students who become embroiled in a murder. It explores themes of morality, obsession, and the consequences of their actions.

Title: A view from the bridge
Author: Arthur Miller
Summary: This play examines the life of an Italian-American longshoreman who struggles with his identity and family loyalty. It explores themes of love, betrayal, and the immigrant experience.

Title: The pearl
Author: John Steinback
Summary: This novella tells the story of a poor pearl diver who finds a valuable pearl, leading to greed and tragedy. It explores themes of wealth, ambition, and the human condition

Title: The warmth of other suns
Author: Isabel Wilkerson
Summary: This book chronicles the Great Migration of African Americans from the South to the North and West between 1915 and 1970. Through personal narratives, it explores the struggles and triumphs of those seeking a better life.

Title: Happy Hour
Author: Marlowe Granados
Summary: This novel follows two young women navigating life, love, and friendship in New York City during a summer filled with parties and adventures. It captures the essence of youth and the bittersweet nature of fleeting moments.

Title: Letters to the father
Author: Franz Kafka
Summary: In this collection of letters, Kafka addresses his father, exploring their complex relationship and his feelings of inadequacy. It reflects on themes of familial bonds, guilt, and the search for understanding.

Title: Tess of the d’ubervilles
Author: Thomas Hardy
Summary: follows Tess, a young woman who faces societal judgment and personal tragedy as she navigates love and loss. It critiques social norms and explores themes of fate and morality.

Title: Anna Karenina
Author: Leo Tolstoy
Summary: This epic novel explores the life of Anna Karenina, a married woman who embarks on a passionate affair with Count Vronsky. The story delves into themes of love, infidelity, and the constraints of society.

Title: Tracks
Author: Louise Erdrich
Summary: This novel weaves together the stories of various characters in a Native American community, exploring themes of identity, heritage, and the impact of history on personal lives.

Title: We can never leave this place
Author: Eric Puchner
Summary: examines the complexities of human relationships and the struggles of modern life, often with a touch of dark humor and poignant insights.

Title: Kafka on the shore
Author: Haruki Murkami
Summary: This novel intertwines the stories of a 15-year-old boy named Kafka and an elderly man named Nakata. It explores themes of memory, identity, and the surreal nature of existence.

Title: Speak
Author: Laurie Halse Anderson
Summary: This novel tells the story of Melinda, a high school freshman who becomes an outcast after a traumatic event. Through her struggle to find her voice, the book addresses themes of trauma, recovery, and the importance of speaking out.

Title: The salt path
Author: Raynor winn
Summary: After losing their home and facing a terminal illness, Raynor and her husband embark on a journey along the South West Coast Path in England. This memoir reflects on resilience, love, and the healing power of nature.

Title: End of watch
Author: Stephen King
Summary: The final installment in the Bill Hodges trilogy, this novel follows retired detective Bill Hodges as he faces off against a psychopathic killer who has returned to wreak havoc. Themes of mortality and the struggle between good and evil are prevalent.

Title: The mysterious disappearance of aidan s
Author: David Levithan
Summary: This story revolves around the sudden disappearance of a teenager named Aidan S. and the impact it has on his friends and family. As they search for answers, they confront their own secrets and the complexities of adolescence.

Title: The life of a stupid man
Author: Ryunosuke Akutagawa
Summary: reflects on the life of a man who struggles with his identity and the absurdity of existence. It delves into themes of self-perception and the search for meaning.

Title: Swanns way
Author: Marcel Proust
Summary: it explores themes of memory, time, and the nature of art through the lens of the narrator's experiences and reflections.

Title: The turn of the screw
Author: Henry James
Summary: follows a governess who becomes convinced that the estate where she works is haunted. It raises questions about perception, reality, and the nature of evil.

Title: Rebecca
Author: Daphne du Maurier
Summary: tells the story of a young woman who marries a wealthy widower, only to find herself haunted by the memory of his first wife, Rebecca. It explores themes of jealousy, identity, and the impact of the past.

Title: The cost of living
Author: Deborah Levy
Summary: examines her life as a woman and writer, addressing themes of loss, independence, and the challenges of navigating personal and professional spaces.

Title: Beyond good and evil
Author: Friedrich Nietzsche
Summary: critiques traditional morality and explores the concept of the "will to power." He challenges readers to reconsider their values and the nature of truth.

Title: One hundred years of solitude
Author: Gabriel García Márquez
Summary: This landmark novel chronicles the Buendía family over several generations in the fictional town of Macondo. It explores themes of solitude, history, and the cyclical nature of life.

Title: Demons
Author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
Summary: explores the themes of nihilism and radicalism in 19th-century Russia through the story of a group of young revolutionaries who plot to overthrow the government, leading to chaos and moral dilemmas.

Title: Giovannis room
Author: James Baldwin
Summary: tells the story of an American man in Paris who grapples with his sexual identity and the complexities of love and desire through his relationship with Giovanni.

Title: Beloved
Author: Toni Morrison
Summary: A haunting narrative about a former enslaved woman who is haunted by the ghost of her deceased daughter, exploring themes of memory, trauma, and the legacy of slavery.

Title: The man who died twice
Author: Lisa Gardner
Summary: A gripping thriller that follows a detective as she investigates a murder case that intertwines with her own past, exploring themes of trauma and redemption.

Title: Concerning the book that is the body of the beloved
Author: Gregory orr
Summary: A philosophical meditation on love and existence, this work explores the relationship between the physical body and the spiritual essence of love.

Title: Bonjour tristesse
Author: Francoise Sagan
Summary: tells the story of a young girl whose carefree summer in the French Riviera is disrupted by her father's romantic entanglements, leading to feelings of sadness and betrayal.

Title: The remains of the day
Author: Kazuo Ishiguro
Summary: about an English butler reflecting on his life and choices, exploring themes of duty, regret, and the passage of time.

Title: The myth of sisyphus
Author: Albert Camus
Summary: discusses the absurdity of life and the human condition, using the myth of Sisyphus as a metaphor for the struggle against meaninglessness.

Title: The unbearable lightness of being
Author: Milan Kundera
Summary: A philosophical exploration of love, politics, and existence, it follows the intertwined lives of several characters in Czechoslovakia during the Prague Spring.

Title: This is how you lose the time war
Author: Amal El-Mohtar and Max Gladstone
Summary: A unique love story told through letters exchanged between two rival agents from different futures, exploring themes of time, love, and the consequences of war.

Title: Song of solomon
Author: Toni Morrison
Summary: explores African American identity through the life of Milkman Dead, who embarks on a journey to discover his family's history and the significance of his heritage.

Title: Intermezzo
Author: Sally Rooney
Summary: captures the complexities of modern relationships, focusing on the emotional intricacies and the impact of societal expectations on personal connections

Title: Everything i never told you
Author: Celeste Ng
Summary: Tells the story of a Chinese-American family dealing with the death of their favorite daughter, exploring themes of race, family expectations, and the pressures of societal norms.

Title: Adolscent
Author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
Summary: follows the life of a young man, Arkady Dolgoruky, as he grapples with his identity, family dynamics, and the complexities of adulthood in a rapidly changing society.

Title: The brothers karamazov
Author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
Summary: delves into deep moral questions through the lives of the Karamazov brothers, exploring themes of faith, doubt, free will, and the nature of evil.

Title: The idiot
Author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
Summary: follows Prince Myshkin, a man whose goodness and open-heartedness clash with the corrupt society around him, leading to tragic consequences as he navigates love and social intrigue.

Title: Their eyes were watching god
Author: Zora Neale Hurston
Summary: follows Janie Crawford's journey to find her voice and independence through her relationships and experiences in early 20th-century Florida.

Title: East of eden
Author: John Steinbeck
Summary: A sprawling narrative that parallels the biblical story of Cain and Abel, it examines themes of good and evil through the lives of two families in California's Salinas Valley.

Title: White Nights
Author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
Summary: tells the story of a lonely man who encounters a young woman during the white nights of St. Petersburg. Their brief but intense relationship explores themes of love, longing, and the complexities of human connection.

Title: Notes From A Dead House
Author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
Summary: Based on Dostoevsky's experiences in a Siberian prison camp, this work offers a poignant reflection on life, suffering, and the human condition. The narrative combines personal anecdotes with philosophical musings, providing insight into the nature of justice and humanity.

Title: Crime and Punishment
Author: Fyodor Dostoyevsky
Summary: follows Raskolnikov, a former student who commits a murder and grapples with guilt and redemption. Dostoevsky delves into moral philosophy, exploring the psychological turmoil of his protagonist and the societal implications of crime.

Title: After shes gone
Author: Camilla Lackberg
Summary: In this gripping mystery, a woman disappears, prompting an investigation that uncovers dark secrets within her family. Lackberg weaves a tale of suspense and psychological depth, exploring themes of love, betrayal, and the complexities of human relationships.

Title: Read people like a book
Author: Patrick King
Summary: teaches readers how to interpret body language and non-verbal cues to better understand others. King provides practical tips and insights into human behavior, emphasizing the importance of empathy and communication in building relationships.

Title: With a mind to kill
Author: Anthony Horowitz
Summary: follows a detective as he investigates a series of murders linked to a high-profile case. Horowitz crafts a complex narrative filled with twists and turns, exploring themes of morality, justice, and the psychological motivations behind crime.

Title: The Family Upstairs
Author: Lisa Jewell
Summary: tells the story of a woman who inherits a house with a dark past, leading her to uncover the secrets of her family's history. Jewell masterfully blends suspense with psychological insights, exploring themes of family dynamics, trauma, and the search for belonging.

Title: The Book You Wish Your Parents Had Read
Author: Philippa Perry
Summary: This book offers insights into parenting and emotional intelligence, encouraging parents to reflect on their own childhood experiences and how these shape their parenting styles. Perry emphasizes the importance of communication and understanding in fostering healthy relationships between parents and children.

Title: Either/or
Author: Elif Batuman
Summary: follows Selin as she navigates her college years, exploring themes of love, identity, and the philosophical dilemmas of choice. Batuman's narrative intertwines personal experiences with literary references, creating a rich tapestry of thought and emotion.

Title: Watching you
Author: Lisa Jewell
Summary: revolves around a young woman who becomes obsessed with her neighbor, leading to a web of secrets and lies. As she uncovers the dark truths about those around her, the story explores themes of obsession, betrayal, and the consequences of watching others.

Title: Animal
Author: Lisa Taddeo
Summary: explores the life of a woman grappling with trauma and the complexities of desire. Taddeo delves into themes of identity, loss, and the search for connection, presenting a raw and emotional narrative that examines the impact of past experiences on present relationships

Title: Thats not my name
Author: Megan Lally
Summary: Shivering and bruised, a teen wakes up on the side of a dirt road with no memory of how she got there―or who she is. A passing officer takes her to the police station, and not long after, a frantic man arrives. He’s been searching for her for hours. He has her school ID, her birth certificate, and even family photos. He is her father. Her name is Mary. Or so he says.

Title: The sudden disappearance of hope
Author: Claire North
Summary: A woman that no one can remember once they stop paying attention to her discovers a conspiracy to control the minds of society's more influential people.

Title: The end of the day
Author: Claire North
Summary: follows the character of Charlie, who works as a "harbinger of death," visiting people on the brink of death. It explores themes of mortality, the meaning of life, and the connections we make with others.

Title: Here we are now
Author: Jasmine Warga
Summary: follows the story of a teenage girl who navigates her complicated relationship with her estranged father while dealing with her own struggles of identity and belonging. It explores themes of family, love, and forgiveness.

Title: Lincoln in the Bardo
Author: George Saunders
Summary: A unique narrative that blends historical fact with fiction, focusing on President Lincoln's grief over the death of his son. The story takes place in a purgatorial setting, exploring themes of loss, love, and the afterlife.

Title: The essays of virginia woolfe
Author: Virginia Woolfe
Summary: A collection of essays exploring various themes such as feminism, literature, and the nature of writing. Woolf's introspective style delves into the complexities of human experience and the role of women in society.

Title: The Bones of you
Author: Debbie Howells
Summary: revolves around the mysterious death of a young girl. The story is told from multiple perspectives, revealing the dark secrets of those involved.

Title: The Waves
Author: Virginia Woolfe
Summary: presents the inner thoughts and experiences of six characters as they navigate life from childhood to adulthood. The narrative is poetic and introspective, reflecting on the nature of identity and human connection.

Title: A room of one’s own
Author: Virginia Woolfe
Summary: An extended essay arguing for both a literal and figurative space for women writers within a patriarchal society. Woolf discusses the importance of financial independence and personal freedom for women to create art.

Title: Mrs. Dalloway
Author: Virginia Woolfe
Summary: follows Clarissa Dalloway as she prepares for a party while reflecting on her past and the choices she has made. It examines themes of mental illness, societal expectations, and the passage of time.

Title: To the lighthouse
Author: Virginia Woolfe
Summary: explores the lives of the Ramsay family during their visits to the Isle of Skye in Scotland. The narrative delves into the characters' inner thoughts and perceptions, reflecting on time, art, and the nature of existence.

Title: The 7 1/2 deaths of evelyn hardcastle
Author: Stuart Turton
Summary: A unique murder mystery where the protagonist relives the same day in different bodies, trying to solve the murder of Evelyn Hardcastle while uncovering dark secrets.

Title: The Haunted House and Other Stories
Author: Virginia Woolfe
Summary: A collection of Woolf's short stories that explore themes of consciousness, identity, and the supernatural.

Title: Two can keep a secret
Author: Karen McManus
Summary: Echo Ridge is small-town America. Ellery’s never been there, but she’s heard all about it. Her aunt went missing there at age seventeen. And only five years ago, a homecoming queen put the town on the map when she was killed. Now Ellery has to move there to live with a grandmother she barely knows

Title: History is all you left me
Author: Adam Silvera
Summary: A poignant story about grief and love, following a boy who navigates his feelings after the death of his first love, exploring themes of memory and loss.

Title: Post office
Author: Charles Bukowski
Summary: Bukowski's experiences working at the post office, reflecting on the absurdities of life and the human condition.

Title: Elsey come home
Author: Susan Conley
Summary: A woman returns to her hometown to confront her past and her family's struggles, exploring themes of belonging and personal growth.

Title: Sense and sensibility
Author: Jane Austen
Summary: The story of the Dashwood sisters as they navigate love, heartbreak, and societal expectations in early 19th-century England.

Title: The midnight library
Author: Matt Haig
Summary: A woman finds herself in a library between life and death, where she can explore alternate lives based on different choices she could have made, leading to profound insights about regret and fulfillment.

Title: Catch and kill
Author: Ronan Farrow
Summary: An exposé of the sexual abuse allegations against powerful men in Hollywood, detailing the lengths to which they went to silence victims and journalists.

Title: More than this
Author: Patrick Ness
Summary: A boy wakes up in a strange place after drowning and must confront his past and the choices he made in life, exploring themes of loss and redemption.

Title: The loop
Author: Ben Oliver
Summary: Set in a dystopian future, the story follows Luka Kane, a teenager imprisoned in The Loop, a facility where juvenile inmates are subjected to torture and medical experiments. As rumors of chaos outside the prison grow, Luka must navigate the dangers within and find a way to escape while uncovering the truth about the world outside.

Title: When all is said
Author: Anne Griffin
Summary: An elderly man reflects on his life and the five toasts he makes to the people who shaped him, exploring themes of love, loss, and memory.

Title: Eleanor oliphant is completely fine
Author: Gail Honeyman
Summary: The story of Eleanor, a socially awkward woman with a traumatic past, who learns to open up and connect with others, leading to personal growth and healing.

Title: Angelas ashes
Author: Frank McCourt
Summary: A poignant memoir of the author's impoverished childhood in Limerick, Ireland, highlighting themes of hardship, family, and resilience.

Title: War and peace
Author: Leo Tolstoy
Summary: intertwines the lives of several families during the Napoleonic Wars, exploring themes of fate, free will, and the nature of history.

Title: Jane Eyre
Author: Charlotte Bronte
Summary: follows the life of Jane Eyre, an orphaned girl who faces hardships and abuse in her childhood. As she grows up, she becomes a governess and falls in love with her employer, Mr. Rochester, only to discover he harbors a dark secret. The story explores themes of love, morality, and social criticism, making it a significant work in feminist literature.

Title: Conversations with friends
Author: Sally Rooney
Summary: follows two college students and their complex relationships with an older married couple, delving into themes of intimacy, friendship, and betrayal.

Title: The starless sea
Author: Erin Morgenstern
Summary: A young man discovers a hidden underground world filled with stories and secrets, exploring themes of love, fate, and the power of storytelling.

Title: Maybe you should talk to someone
Author: Lori Gottlieb
Summary: A therapist shares her experiences with her patients and her own therapy, offering insights into the human condition and the complexities of mental health.

Title: Colorless Tsukuru Tazaki
Author: Haruki Murakami
Summary: follows Tsukuru Tazaki, a man who feels disconnected from his past and his friends after they abruptly cut ties with him. As he embarks on a journey to understand why, he confronts themes of loneliness, identity, and the impact of relationships

Title: Lost in the Never Woods
Author: Aiden Thomas
Summary: retelling of Peter Pan follows Wendy as she navigates the mysteries of her past and the disappearance of children in her town. It explores themes of loss, memory, and the transition to adulthood.

Title: The Invisible Life of Addie LaRue
Author: V.E. Schwab
Summary: follows Addie LaRue, a young woman who makes a deal to live forever but is cursed to be forgotten by everyone she meets. It explores themes of identity, love, and the desire for legacy.

Title: The Afterlife of Holly Chase
Author: Cynthia Hand
Summary: This modern retelling of "A Christmas Carol" follows Holly Chase, a girl who is visited by ghosts after her death. She must confront her past and the choices that led to her demise.

Title: One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich
Author: Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn
Summary: This novella depicts a single day in the life of Ivan Denisovich Shukhov, a prisoner in a Soviet labor camp. It highlights the struggle for dignity and humanity in the face of oppressive conditions.

Title: 101 Essays That Will Change the Way You Think
Author: Brianna Wiest
Summary: Offers insights and reflections on various aspects of life, encouraging readers to rethink their perspectives and embrace change.

Title: Dowry of Blood
Author: S.T. Gibson
Summary: This reimagining of the Dracula mythos focuses on Constanta, who reflects on her tumultuous relationship with Dracula and the other brides. The narrative explores themes of love, power, and the complexities of toxic relationships.

Title: A Tale of Two Cities
Author: Charles Dickens
Summary: Set during the tumultuous times of the French Revolution, this novel tells the story of Charles Darnay and Sydney Carton, two men who love the same woman, Lucie Manette. It explores themes of sacrifice, resurrection, and the effects of social injustice

Title: The One
Author: John Marrs
Summary: imagines a world where a DNA test can find your perfect romantic match. As various characters navigate their relationships, the story explores the implications of love, fate, and choice.

Title: The Mountain Is You
Author: Brianna Wiest
Summary: explores the concept of self-sabotage and how individuals can overcome their internal obstacles to achieve personal growth and fulfillment.

Title: Dead Souls
Author: Nikolay Gogol
Summary: follows Chichikov, a man who travels through Russia buying the "dead souls" of deceased serfs to increase his social standing. It satirizes the moral and social issues of 19th-century Russia.

Title: Murder
Author: Kate Morgan
Summary: delves into various murder cases, exploring the psychological profiles of the killers and the circumstances surrounding their crimes.

Title: If We Were Villains
Author: M.L. Rio
Summary: follows a group of Shakespearean actors at an elite arts college whose lives become intertwined with a murder mystery. It explores themes of friendship, ambition, and the blurred lines between performance and reality

Title: The Dreamers
Author: Karen Thompson Walker
Summary: In a small town, a mysterious illness causes people to fall into a deep sleep from which they cannot awaken. The novel explores the impact of this phenomenon on the community and the nature of dreams and reality.

Title: The Seven Husbands of Evelyn Hugo
Author: Taylor Jenkins Reid
Summary: tells the story of Evelyn Hugo, a reclusive Hollywood icon, who recounts her glamorous and tumultuous life, including her seven marriages, to a young journalist. It explores themes of love, identity, and the price of fame.

Title: Valley of the Dolls
Author: Jacqueline Susann
Summary: This novel chronicles the lives of three women navigating the entertainment industry in the 1960s, dealing with love, addiction, and the pursuit of happiness.

Title: Her body and other parties
Author: Carme Maria Machado
Summary: Blends horror and fantasy, exploring the female experience and the complexities of identity, sexuality, and trauma

Title: Suicide notes from beautiful girls
Author: Lynn Weingarten
Summary: This novel follows the story of a girl named June who investigates the mysterious death of her best friend, Delia. As she uncovers secrets, the narrative explores themes of friendship, betrayal, and mental health.

Title: The picture of Dorian Gray
Author: Oscar Wilde
Summary: Tells the story of Dorian Gray, a young man whose portrait ages while he remains youthful. It explores themes of vanity, moral corruption, and the consequences of a life devoted to pleasure.

Title: Those who leave and those who stay
Author: Elena Ferrante
Summary: The third installment of the Neapolitan Quartet, this novel delves into the lives of Lila and Elena as they confront their choices and the impact of their past on their present lives.

Title: The story of a new name
Author: Elena Ferrante
Summary: Ffocusing on the lives of childhood friends Lila and Elena as they navigate adulthood, marriage, and the challenges of their evolving identities.

Title: Just kids
Author: Patti Smith
Summary: Recounts Smith's relationship with photographer Robert Mapplethorpe in New York City during the 1960s and 70s. It captures their artistic journey and the deep bond they shared, set against the backdrop of a vibrant cultural scene.

Title: The happy prisoner
Author: Monica Dickens
Summary: Explores the concept of happiness within the confines of a prison, examining the psychological aspects of finding joy and meaning in difficult circumstances.

Title: Everything I know about love
Author: Dolly Alderton
Summary: In this memoir, Alderton reflects on her experiences with love, friendship, and growing up. Through humorous and poignant anecdotes, she shares the lessons learned from her relationships and the importance of self-love.

Title: The bell jar
Author: Sylvia plath
Summary: This semi-autobiographical novel follows Esther Greenwood, a young woman who struggles with mental illness and societal expectations in 1950s America. The narrative explores her descent into depression and her experiences in a psychiatric hospital.

Title: Metamorphosis
Author: Franz Kafka
Summary: Tells the story of Gregor Samsa, who wakes up one morning to find himself transformed into a giant insect. It explores themes of alienation, identity, and the absurdity of life.

Title: Homesick for another world
Author: Ottessa Moshfegh
Summary: Explores the lives of various characters grappling with loneliness, desire, and the search for meaning in a contemporary world.

Title: Sharp objects
Author: Gillan Flynn
Summary: Follows journalist Camille Preaker as she returns to her hometown to cover a series of murders. As she investigates, she confronts her own traumatic past and the dark secrets of her family.

Title: The stranger
Author: Alburt Camus
Summary: Follows Meursault, a man who becomes embroiled in a murder trial after killing an Arab. It explores themes of absurdism, morality, and the human condition.

Title: Marly‘s ghost
Author: David Levithan
Summary: Follows Marlys, a young girl who navigates the complexities of adolescence, family, and identity, blending humor and poignant moments.

Title: The art of war
Author: Sun Tzu
Summary: This ancient Chinese text is a treatise on military strategy and tactics. It emphasizes the importance of adaptability, strategy, and understanding one's enemy.

Title: The art of unspoken longing
Author: Philippe Benson
Summary: Presumably a lyrical and emotionally rich novel or poetry collection centered around yearning, silence, and the pain of unexpressed love.

Title: Pleasure
Author: Gabriele D’Annunzio
Summary: A lush, sensual novel about a decadent Italian nobleman torn between two women. Rich in aestheticism and philosophical musings, it captures the spirit of fin-de-siècle hedonism and existential crisis.

Title: Kill Your Darlings
Author: Messermoon
Summary: A modern, introspective take on obsession, creativity, and toxic relationships within an elite academic setting.

Title: Madonna in a fur coat
Author: Sabahattin Ali
Summary: A melancholic love story set in 1920s Berlin, where a reserved Turkish man falls for an enigmatic German artist. Themes of loneliness, identity, and longing permeate this poignant tale.

Title: In the Absence of Men
Author: Philippe Besson
Summary: Set in World War I France, a young man falls in love with an older man while developing a friendship with Marcel Proust. A lyrical tale of first love, desire, and social constraints.

Title: Love is a Dog from Hell
Author: Charles Bukowski
Summary: Exploring love, loneliness, sex, and heartbreak. Bukowski’s voice is vulgar yet vulnerable, portraying relationships with unflinching honesty.

Title: The Tell-Tale Heart
Author: Edgar Allan Poe
Summary: Madness and guilt, where the narrator insists on his sanity while recounting the murder he committed. The incessant beating of the dead man’s heart drives him to confess.

Title: Cursed Bread
Author: Sophie Mackintosh
Summary: A reimagining of the real-life 1951 mass poisoning in Pont-Saint-Esprit, France. Told from the perspective of a baker’s wife obsessed with a glamorous general’s wife, the novel explores repression, female desire, madness, and collective hysteria.

Title: I Remain in Darkness
Author: Annie Ernaux
Summary: Nobel laureate Annie Ernaux documents her mother’s decline from Alzheimer’s disease. A raw, intimate portrayal of loss, memory, and the emotional toll of caregiving.

Title: Cold Enough for Snow
Author: Jessica Au
Summary: A quiet, introspective novel about a woman traveling to Japan with her mother. It reflects on memory, identity, art, and the unbridgeable distance between people—even those closest to us.

Title: Hollow Heart
Author: Viola Di Grado
Summary: A surreal and haunting novel told from the perspective of a young woman who has died by suicide and continues to narrate her life in the afterlife. It explores alienation, depression, and the border between life and death.

Title: Thirst for Salt
Author: Madelaine Lucas
Summary: Set on the coast of Australia, this debut novel tells of a young woman’s passionate summer affair with an older man. Through lush prose, it navigates love, memory, longing, and the complexities of human connection.

Title: Case Study
Author: Graeme Macrae Burnet
Summary: A woman investigates a controversial psychotherapist by pretending to be a patient. Blurring lines between fiction and reality, it explores themes of identity, mental illness, and narrative truth.

Title: This Thing Between Us
Author: Gus Moreno
Summary: A grieving husband spirals into paranoia and supernatural dread after his wife’s death, blurring trauma with horror.

Title: Orpheus Builds a Girl
Author: Heather Parry
Summary: A haunting reimagining of the Orpheus myth, exploring grief, obsession, and the disturbing creation of an “ideal” woman.

Title: The Dispossessed
Author: Ursula K. Le Guin
Summary: A physicist navigates two contrasting societies, examining freedom, capitalism, and anarchism.

Title: Dead Girls Don’t Talk But This One Does
Author: Sandra J. Paul
Summary: A dark, introspective narrative about trauma, violence, and the lingering voice of a victim.

Title: The Book of Disquiet
Author: Fernando Pessoa
Summary: Fragmented reflections on identity, existence, and alienation from a melancholic Lisbon bookkeeper.

Title: The Lost Estate
Author: Alain-Fournier
Summary: A nostalgic tale of lost youth and unattainable love centered around a mysterious woman and a fleeting paradise.

Title: Nightwood
Author: Djuna Barnes
Summary: A dense, poetic exploration of destructive love, identity, and emotional ruin.

Title: Lolita
Author: Vladimir Nabokov
Summary: A deeply disturbing yet stylistically brilliant account of obsession and manipulation narrated by an unreliable predator.

Title: Journey to the End of the Night
Author: Louis-Ferdinand Céline
Summary: A bleak, cynical journey through war, colonialism, and modern life’s moral decay.

Title: The Night Circus
Author: Erin Morgenstern
Summary: Two magicians bound in a lifelong competition fall in love within a magical, dreamlike circus.

Title: Confessions of Saint Augustine
Author: Maria Boulding for beauty and poetry/ Thomas williams for accuracy
Summary: A spiritual autobiography exploring sin, faith, and the search for divine truth.

Title: Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil
Author: John Berendt
Summary: A real-life murder case in Savannah intertwined with eccentric Southern characters.

Title: First Love
Author: Ivan Turgenev
Summary: A young man experiences the bittersweet pain of first love and emotional awakening.

Title: Down Below
Author: Leonora Carrington
Summary: A surreal memoir of the author’s mental breakdown and institutionalization.

Title: Paradise Lost
Author: John Milton
Summary: An epic poem depicting the fall of Satan and humanity, grappling with free will, sin, and redemption.

Title: The Last Days of Socrates
Author: Plato
Summary: Dialogues recounting Socrates’ trial, imprisonment, and reflections on justice and death.

Title: The Collected Schizophrenia
Author: Esmé Weijun Wang
Summary: Essays detailing life with schizophrenia and the complexity of mental illness.

Title: The Divine Comedy V3: Paradise
Author: Dante Alighieri
Summary: Dante ascends through Heaven, guided by Beatrice, encountering souls in states of perfect bliss and gaining deeper understanding of divine love, justice, and the ultimate harmony of the universe.

Title: The Divine Comedy v2: Purgatory
Author: Dante Alighieri
Summary: Souls ascend toward redemption, reflecting hope and spiritual purification.

Title: The Divine Comedy V1: Inferno
Author: Dante Alighieri
Summary: A journey through Hell, symbolizing sin, justice, and moral consequence.

Title: The Complete Poetry of John Milton
Author: John T. Shawcross (ed.)
Summary: A collection of Milton’s works exploring religion, morality, and human struggle.

Title: Midnight Sailing
Author: Susan Hufford
Summary: A quiet, emotional story centered on love, longing, and personal reflection.

Title: The Late Mattia Pascal
Author: Luigi Pirandello
Summary: A man assumes a new identity after being declared dead, questioning selfhood and freedom.

Title: The Penguin Book of the Undead
Author: Scott G. Bruce (ed.)
Summary: Historical accounts and writings on encounters with the undead across cultures.

Title: The Daughters of Music
Author: Susannah Lawrence
Summary: A story of ambition, relationships, and emotional entanglements within artistic life.

Title: Dance in the Dust
Author: Denise Robins
Summary: A dramatic love story shaped by passion, hardship, and societal expectations.

Title: The Time of Indifference
Author: Alberto Moravia
Summary: A family’s emotional detachment exposes moral emptiness and societal decay.

Title: The Intruder
Author: Gabriele D’Annunzio
Summary: A story of betrayal, jealousy, and obsessive love.

Title: Zeno’s Conscience
Author: Italo Svevo
Summary: A man’s therapy sessions reveal self-deception, addiction, and existential confusion.

Title: The Leopard
Author: Giuseppe Tomasi di Lampedusa
Summary: A Sicilian prince reflects on change, decay, and mortality during political upheaval.

Title: Diavola
Author: Jennifer Thorne
Summary: A tense, eerie narrative blending family tension with psychological unease.

Title: The Swan Thieves
Author: Elizabeth Kostova
Summary: A psychiatrist uncovers a painter’s obsession tied to art, love, and history.

Title: The Man Who Watched the Trains Go By
Author: Georges Simenon
Summary: A man abandons his life and descends into crime and existential crisis.

Title: Resurrection
Author: Leo Tolstoy
Summary: A nobleman seeks redemption after recognizing his role in a woman’s suffering.

Title: The Essential Writings of Christian Mysticism
Author: Bernard McGinn (ed.)
Summary: Key texts exploring divine experience, spirituality, and inner transformation.

Title: The Anatomy of Melancholy
Author: Robert Burton
Summary: A vast exploration of depression, its causes, and human emotion.

Title: Chernobyl Prayer
Author: Svetlana Alexievich
Summary: Oral histories revealing the human cost and trauma of the Chernobyl disaster.

Title: How to Read a Film
Author: James Monaco
Summary: A guide to understanding film language, theory, and visual storytelling.

Title: On Sun Swallowing
Author: Dakota Warren
Summary: A poetic exploration of grief, identity, and emotional fragmentation.

Title: The Woman Destroyed
Author: Simone de Beauvoir
Summary: Stories of women confronting betrayal, aging, and emotional collapse.

Title: The Rotting Room
Author: Viggy Parr Hampton
Summary: A dark, unsettling narrative exploring decay, confinement, and mental deterioration.

Title: Morbid Curiosities: Collections of the Uncommon and the Bizarre
Author: Paul Gambino
Summary: A richly illustrated exploration of unusual collectors and collections, featuring medical oddities, taxidermy, crime memorabilia, and historical curiosities that reveal humanity’s fascination with the macabre.

Title: A Delusion of Satan: The Full Story of the Salem Witch Trials
Author: Frances Hill
Summary: A detailed account of the Salem witch trials, exploring how fear, religious extremism, and social tensions fueled one of America’s most infamous episodes of mass hysteria.

Title: Demons, the Devil, and Fallen Angels
Author: Marie D. Jones & Larry Flaxman
Summary: An accessible survey of demonic figures and beliefs across religions, mythologies, and paranormal traditions, examining humanity’s enduring fear of evil entities.

Title: Cassell Dictionary of Superstitions
Author: David Pickering
Summary: An extensive guide to superstitions from around the world, tracing their origins, meanings, and cultural significance across centuries.

Title: The World, the Flesh, and the Devil: A Biographical Dictionary of Witches
Author: Eric Maple
Summary: A reference work documenting accused witches, occult practitioners, and legendary figures associated with witchcraft throughout European history and folklore.
